title: Education curriculum includes CPR, first aid
summary: Life-saving cardiopulmonary resuscitation, first aid and basic life support training have been integrated across the basic education curriculum to equip students with the confidence and skills needed…

blocks.text: In a statement, DepEd Secretary Sonny Angara emphasized that teaching life-saving skills is fundamentally about protecting loved ones and caring for one another in critical moments.

MANILA, Philippines — Life-saving cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR), first aid and basic life support training have been integrated across the basic education curriculum to equip students with the confidence and skills needed to assist in emergencies, the Department of Education said yesterday.

DepEd said Republic Act 10871, commonly known as the Samboy Lim Law, is embedded across basic education through the Revised K-10 Physical Education and Health curriculum and the strengthened senior high school (SHS) program.
The curriculum establishes a progressive, age-appropriate learning continuum from elementary through SHS.

Elementary learners in Grades 4 to 6 start with foundational safety awareness and basic injury prevention. In junior high school, learners build on these basics by mastering first aid principles and immediate care for common injuries, environmental emergencies and road and water safety. By Grade 10, learners gain practical training in basic life support and emergency care procedures.

In SHS, subject to school offerings and partner programs, learners undergo training in responder-level skills, such as compression-only CPR, automated external defibrillator operation, rescue breathing, foreign body airway obstruction maneuvers and mass casualty response protocols, with an opportunity to earn official certification from recognized and accredited health organizations.

“We are working to provide hands-on training for our teachers and ensure that schools are adequately equipped, ultimately aiming for a point where helping others and sustaining life becomes second nature to every student,” Angara said.

DepEd encouraged Schools Division offices to maximize available local funds and build public-private and community partnerships, such as with the Department of Health, local government units and accredited health organizations, to standardize training, expand access to life-support equipment and help schools and communities respond promptly during emergencies.
